text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended broadly mixed, with nearby months posting heavy losses in a late sell-off on sharp falls in New York. July lost $60 to close at $1,840 per tonne, while September closed $45 easier at $1,865 per tonne. The July/September spread which narrowed to $4 at one stage widened again to end at $25.

Arabica futures in New York tumbled as a late-session round of local and speculative selling drove the benchmark September contract to its lowest settlement since April 22. July lost 18.65 cents/lb to close at 190.05 cents/lb, while September gave up 15.15 cents/lb to close at 175.55 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 8.65 and 12.15 cents/lb. The July/September switch fell to 14.50 cents from 18.00 cents the previous day.

There were no fresh fundamental news although the USDA estimate for 1997/98 continued to weigh on the market. The USDA estimated that Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop could reach 28 million 60-kg bags, up from a revised 27.5 million in 1996/97. USDA pegged world 1997/98 production at 103.7 million versus 100.7 million in 1996/97. The estimate for Brazil was heavily criticized by government sources and Mauricio Assis, head of the Primary Commodities Department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry, said the USDA should have explained how it reached its figure.

USDA defended the forecast, saying the high number reflected a number of factors including generally good growing conditions, the increased number of bearing trees and sharply higher prices than a year ago. Assis said coffee production would drop sharply in the states of Minas Gerais and Espirito Santo in 1997/98, improve significantly in Parana and remain roughly the same in Sao Paulo. He added that in most producing areas the low-production cycle is occurring.
UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 264 bags on June 17 to 47,286 bags, down from 47,550 bags the previous day and 48,050 bags on June 13.

FRANCE - France imported 653,932 bags of coffee in March 1997, 15 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 to 1.867 million bags, 12 percent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 7 percent to 6.696 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Brazil (283,300 vs 174,900 bags) and Colombia (137,700 vs 163,000 bags).

The country exported 311,700 bags of coffee in January/March 1997, 13 percent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 10 percent to 1.186 million bags.

JAPAN - Japan imported 524,081 bags of coffee in March 1997, 26 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 to 1.455 million bags, 23 percent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 5.5 percent to 5.619 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Brazil (323,600 vs 212,800 bags), Colombia (325,400 vs 294,400 bags) and Indonesia (228,500 vs 191,400 bags).
